description: THE SAFETY REGRESSION. Uses REAL KashiGRC codes. The policy is entirely about encryption, and the catalogue offered contains only HRS and TPR controls — CRY-01.x and CRY-02.x are deliberately withheld. A model reaching for a plausible ISO clause from memory, or for a CRY code it saw during training on this catalogue, fails here. Run on every prompt change without exception.

variables.policyText: All customer data is encrypted at rest using AES-256 and in transit using TLS 1.2 or above. Cryptographic keys are held in AWS KMS, rotated annually, and access to key material is restricted to the platform engineering team. Key generation, storage, and destruction follow documented procedures.

description: Counterweight to 001. A guard tuned so tightly that nothing is ever suggested is also a failure. Real HRS controls, a policy that genuinely satisfies HRS-01.1 and HRS-02.1.

variables.policyText: All new joiners complete background verification before receiving system access. Every employee signs an NDA and confidentiality terms as part of their employment contract. Staff complete security awareness training within 14 days of joining and annually thereafter, tracked by the Head of Security.

description: DOMAIN and FAMILY nodes are navigational, not evidenceable. A suggestion of 'IAM — Identity & Access Management' is true, useless, and impossible to evidence. candidateControls() filters to NodeLevel.CONTROL; this proves the model does not reintroduce parents from the codes it sees in the leaf names.

variables.policyText: Access is granted on documented manager approval through Okta. Role changes trigger an entitlement update within two business days. Leaver access is revoked within four hours of the HR exit trigger. Entitlements are reviewed quarterly by system owners.
